acceptance.criterion: The whole module still compiles after the test-file changes
The claim CLI package and the RPC packages pass together, so the literal exit-code assertions and the renamed-op metrics check hold on both sides of the wire
Both end-to-end exit-code tests (direct mode and daemon mode) run and pass in the default gate, with no build tag hiding them
The full test suite is green, including the new package-level TestMain in cmd/bd

findings.what: cmd/bd/claim_test.go:355 and :414 compared the observed denial exit status against claimDeniedExit, the package's own constant, so the exit-3 contract was unasserted.
findings.fix: Both assertions now compare against the literal 3 (claim_test.go:375 direct mode, :440 daemon mode); claimDeniedExit appears only inside the failure message text.

findings.what: Audited the whole file for the same pattern. Two further instances: assertDaemonServedClaims matched the daemon's metrics row on rpc.OpClaim (a rename would have kept the test green), and TestClaimFlagsTruncatesSubSecondRemainder cross-checked the RPC lease against the value claimFlags itself returned.
findings.fix: The metrics loop now matches the literal wire name "claim" (constant named only in the comment and the failure message); the truncation test asserts the literal 90 seconds. The remaining uses of types.* and rpc.* constants in the file are test inputs, not expected values, and were left alone. Also split two `x == nil || *x != want` guards into a nil Fatal plus a value Errorf, because the combined form printed a pointer address instead of the observed number on failure.

findings.what: claimTestBinary built the 33 MB bd binary into an os.MkdirTemp directory nothing removed, leaking 33 MB per `go test ./cmd/bd/` run.
findings.fix: The sync.Once now records the directory in claimBinaryDir, and a new package-level TestMain (claim_test.go:237) removes it after m.Run() returns, before os.Exit, so the removal happens whether the tests pass or fail. cmd/bd had no prior TestMain.

findings.what: The `strings.Contains(res.stderr, "direct mode")` fallback guard in TestClaimExitCodesInDaemonMode caught only the unconditional auto-start-timeout warning (daemon_autostart.go:309); the connect-failed and health-failed fallbacks print via emitVerboseWarning (daemon_autostart.go:411), which main.go:739 gates on BD_VERBOSE, which the test did not set.
findings.fix: The daemon test's environment is now {BEADS_NO_DAEMON=0, BD_VERBOSE=1}, so every fallback reason prints (all of the emitVerboseWarning messages contain the substring "direct mode"). The comment now says the guard fails fast on a fallback and names assertDaemonServedClaims (the daemon's own operation counters) as the primary proof that the RPC route ran.

Failure path also checked: with claimDeniedExit mutated to 1 so the run FAILED, the cleanup still left 0 directories.

notes: Only cmd/bd/claim_test.go is modified in the commit, matching the bead's Touches allowlist. All mutations were to files outside the allowlist and were restored before the gate ran; `git status --porcelain` showed only ` M cmd/bd/claim_test.go` before `bdc`, and is empty after.

The 23 accumulated /tmp/bd-claim-e2e-* directories the bead cites are shared across every worktree of this repo; new ones appeared during this session from a sibling builder running the pre-fix test file, which is why the leak check was done under an isolated TMPDIR.
